conclusion: Across 89 out-of-time company-year forecasts, next-year operating-cash-flow MAE was 3.08% of opening assets for cash persistence and 3.07% for the accrual model.

comparison.title: One-year-ahead cash-flow forecasts
comparison.unit: Mean absolute error (% of target year's opening assets)
comparison.note: Each fitted model sees only labels publicly filed before the forecast.

slice.title: Does the cash advantage persist by year?
slice.note: Negative values mean the accrual model lost to cash persistence.

sensitivity.title: Apple residual-income sensitivity
sensitivity.note: Scenario valuation holds book fixed under full payout. The cost of equity and persistence are assumptions.

valuation.collection_assumptions: One-time year-one loss as a fraction of trade receivables with other cash flows and full-payout baseline held fixed; no tax shield.

audit.audited_note: Apple FY2023 Form 10-K, printed page 38: vendor non-trade receivables arise from components supplied to manufacturing vendors. The two largest counterparties accounted for 48% and 23%. Audit trade and vendor receivables separately before interpreting collections.
audit.chronology: New annual originals only for forecast features. Later amended or repeated comparative values are retained separately for auditing.

next_decision: Investigate persistent cash-collection gaps alongside the audited note, industry and fiscal period. Use issuer-specific balance-sheet classifications before applying a valuation haircut.

study_design.protocol: Use a preselected set of 24 nonfinancial issuers. Retain filing dates and accessions, identify first original 10-K observations, and preserve later comparisons and amendments separately. Align annual income and CFO with point-in-time balances. Compare earnings/CFO persistence and a regularized working-capital decomposition using only matured prior labels. Include an issuer-held-out fit, annual falsification and a residual-income valuation sensitivity anchored to book value.

data.grain: One issuer, accession and fiscal period in an original or comparative annual filing
